lit.\u0027¿Qué aminoácido tiene una cadena l: "Which amino acid has an acidic side chain?"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003epI\u003c/b\u003e: pH: "pI: pH of net charge 0; below it the molecule is a cation, above it an anion."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon pH creciente cada:
"

With increasing pH each group loses its proton when pH > pKa (Henderson–Hasselbalch). Here, aspartate: α-COOH (1.88), side-chain COOH (3.65) and α-NH₃⁺ (9.60). The isoelectric point is the pH of net charge 0: the average of the two pKa values surrounding the neutral form, pI = (1.88 + 3.65)/2 = 2.77.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon φ ≈ −120° y ψ ≈ +:
"

With φ ≈ −120° and ψ ≈ +130° the backbone extends in a zigzag (≈ 3.3 Å per residue). Two antiparallel strands are joined by H bonds between the C=O and N–H groups of neighboring strands; the side chains alternate above and below the pleated plane.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon φ ≈ −57° y ψ ≈ −4:
"

With φ ≈ −57° and ψ ≈ −47° the backbone coils into a right-handed helix of 3.6 residues per turn and a 5.4 Å pitch. Each C=O forms a hydrogen bond (≈ 2 Å) with the N–H of residue i+4 (yellow lines). The side chains point outward.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl grupo α-COOH de un:
"

The α-COOH group of one amino acid reacts with the α-NH₂ of another and releases water. The C–N bond (1.33 Å) has partial double-bond character by resonance: the six atoms (Cα, C, O, N, H, Cα) lie in a rigid plane with ω ≈ 180° (trans).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos ángulos \u003cb\u:
"

The angles φ (N–Cα) and ψ (Cα–C) are the only degrees of freedom of the backbone. Many combinations produce steric clashes (red): the allowed regions correspond to α-helix, β-sheet/PPII and, less frequently, left-handed helix. It is calculated here with a simple hard-sphere model.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eSe clasifican en \u00:
"

They are classified as nonpolar (Gly, Ala, Val, Leu, Ile, Met, Phe, Pro, Trp), polar uncharged (Ser, Thr, Cys, Tyr, Asn, Gln), acidic (Asp, Glu) and basic (Lys, Arg, His). Go through some representative ones.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eα-ami:
"

An α-amino acid has an α carbon bound to an amino group, a carboxyl group, an H and a side chain (R). At physiological pH it exists as a zwitterion: –NH₃⁺ and –COO⁻. All proteinogenic ones (except glycine, which is achiral) are L (S configuration, except cysteine which is R because of CIP priorities).

"
